entry.title: Web Dev
Express vs Fastify vs NestJS
entry.content:
Express vs Fastify vs NestJS

  • Express - slow + unstructured.
  • Fastify - fast + unstructured.
  • NestJS - slow + structured.
  • NestJS + Fastify - moderately slow + structured, using fastify.

    For large projects w/ nestjs, using fastify along w/ it does no much performance improvement.

entry.title: 09. Advanced K8s
entry.content:
Advanced K8s (Story Based)

Devops
|-- K8s
    |-- K8s Fundamentals
    |-- Application packaging
    |    |-- helm
    |    |-- charts
    |    |-- values.yaml
    |    |-- chart.yaml
    |    |-- helm repositories
    |-- Gitops
    |    |-- Argo CD
    |    |-- Applications
    |    |-- Application sets
    |    |-- SyncReconciliation
    |    |-- Drift detection
    |    |-- Git as source of truth
    |-- Continuous delivery (CD)
        |-- Progressive Delivery
        |-- Rollbacks
        |-- Automated deployments
  • Without helm
    • Suppose you have multiple services like frontend, backend, postgres, redis, ingress, etc. For each one will have to write deployment.yaml, service.yaml, ingress.yaml, configmap.yaml, secret.yaml, pvc.yaml, etc.
    • This results in 20, 30, 50 yamls… For deploying in different environments like dev & prod we will have to copy that files multiple times.
    • Too much work, duplicate files.
  • With helm
    • Reduced duplication via templates
    • Thus, it is most useful when used in combination w/ template expressions like `` But one can run “helm install myapp” without template expressions just with static data though it is same.(Running above mentioned command is called as installing a helm chart or installing a release.)
    • Template files (with template expressions) are called value files
  • Value files
    • To deploy different kinds of values to different environments (Eg: values-dev.yaml)
    • Avoid duplicated manifests while still maintaining operationBinding to k8s env file, but w/o security.
  • Charts.yaml
    • Addition of it to any folder makes that folder a valid “chart” & makes helm recognise it as one installable package.
    • Running “helm install myrelease my-app” (Installing a helm chart / release)
    • In general, we don’t push charts (folder created w/ charts.yaml) into OCI registries (open w/ charts.yaml) into OCI registries (open w/ charts.yaml). It is just spun on the repos required nodes.
    • But in general, we push to OCI registries same as docker images (Eg: dockerhub, github container registry, Amazon ECR, Google artifact registry, Azure container registry).
  • Multiple charts
    • by having multiple folders ref chart.yaml to install.
  • Third party charts
    • to install, popular reusable packages/charts like prometheus, grafana, etc. redis, postgres, etc.
    • Installing multiple helm charts
      • Helm file
        • used for describing multiple helm releases in one place, or deploying them together & volatile controlling, ordering & shared configuration.
  • Gitops / ArgoCD
    • Subset of DevOps.
    • Focuses on keeping DevOps in sync across teams in large organizations.Git as source of truth
    • A tool used for that is ArgoCD.
      • ArgoCD is a CRD so running in K8s.
      • Entire setup for argo CD as manifests.
      • ArgoCD watches for changes and sunsets them if necessary.Something like protecting dev/main branches in github/gitlab.
      • Argo Project consists of argocd, argo workflows, argo rollouts, argo events.
        • Named after mythological ship Argonauts - Logo of argo is an orange squid.

entry.title: SSE vs Websocket
entry.content:
SSE vs Websocket

(Rest api still always better than these open connections)

  • SSE
    • Server sent events.
    • way for server to continuously push updates to a client via HTTP. one-way
    • switch (notification, live dashboard, logs, tokens)
  • Web socket
    • continuous message from both client and server.
  • both use an open connection (not polling). SSE uses HTTP connection. websocket starts as HTTP and then upgraded to websocket protocol where messages are exchanged as websocket frames. (chat apps, game, collab editing)

entry.title: DNS and TLS/SSL
entry.content:
DNS and TLS/SSL

  • DNS
    • Domain naming system
    • assigns registering a static IP of a website and buying a domain name.
  • TLS
    • transport layer security.
    • encrypts data sent b/w client & server.
    • modern version of ssl (secure sockets layer)
    • HTTP + TLS = HTTPS.

entry.title: Load Balancing And Traffic Management
entry.content:
load balancing

  • Round robin
    • load distributed sequentially & evenly across available servers.
    • Eg: 
      upstream backend {
  server app1 : 3000;
  server app2 : 3000;
  }
  • weighted load balancing
    • you weight servers. % wise
    • Eg: 
      upstream backend {
  server app1 : 3000
  weight = 3;
  server app2 : 300
  weight = 1;
  }
    • app 1 get 75% more traffic.
  • least connections
    • traffic to least busy instance.
    • Eg: 
      upstream backend {
  least_conn;
  server app1 : 3000;
  server app2 : 3000;
  }
  • Health check/failover
    • if app dies, traffic moves to app2.
    • Eg: 
      upstream backend {
  server app1 : 3000
  max_fails = 3
  fail_timeout = 30s
  server app2 : 3000;
  }
  • sticky session load balancing 
    upstream backend {
    ip_hashserver ...
    }
upstream backend {
    sticky cookie srv_id expires = 1h;
    server apps ...
    }
    • can be based on IP or cookies etc.
    • not a load balancing algo, but rather a constraint that modifies load balancing behaviour.

entry.title: Istio Ingress
entry.content:
Istio-ingress

  • An alternative to nginx ingress.
  • Ingress fundamentals:
    • K8s ingress (needs an ingress controller like nginx, traefik, HAProxy, etc.).
    • Focused on layer 7 (HTTP) routing.
      • Nginx is said to be basic layer 7 routing. Istio is a advanced layer 7 routing b/c it provides much more than nginx through at layer 7, like traffic splitting, canary deployments, retry policies, circuit breakers, mTLS, observability, fault injection.
      • Layers (Comp. Sci network model term)
        • 3 Network models :- OSI Model, TCP/IP Model, Hybrid TCP/IP model.
        • OSI model
          • created by ISO.
          • OSI (Open Systems Interconnection)
          • ISO (Internal Organisation for Standardisation)
      • 7 layers conceptual model. Not used in real world. Used by k8s for theory purpose.
      • 7 model:
        • layer 7 - application
        • layer 6 - presentation
        • layer 5 - session
        • layer 4 - transport
        • layer 3 - network
        • layer 2 - data link
        • layer 1 - physical.
      • layer details:
        • Application
          • user facing
          • HTTP, HTTPS, DNS etc
        • Presentation
          • data format, encryption encoding
          • TLS/SSL, PNG/JPEG, UTF8, ASCII
        • Session
          • connection, session management
          • SMB Session, TLS session, Net BIOS
        • transport
          • End to end communication
          • TCP, UDP, QUIC,
        • network - routing - IP (v4/v6), ICMP
        • Data link
          • communication on same n/w
          • ethernet, wifi, VLAN, MAC address
        • Physical
          • Actual signal transmission
          • copper cables, fibre optic, etc.
      • TCP/IP model:-
        • only 4 layers. used in reality
        • layers include:- Application, transport, internet & n/w access
        • hybrid:
          • has 5 layers
          • application, transport, network, data link, physical
        • other vendor specific layer models that are not commonly used by anyone:
  • Istio-ingress
    • Istio
      • service mesh platform.
      • Contains controlplane (istiod), side car proxies (envoy), traffic management, mTLS, authorization policies, observability, ingress gateway, egres gateway all w/o touching the app.
      • uses istio-ingress gateway which was envoy.
      • envoy, is a proxy that forwards requests, load balancer, TLS termination, metrics, collection, traffic splitting, etc.
  • Other ingress fundamentals
    • north south traffic - traffic to and from outside the app
    • east west traffic - traffic within services of the app internals
    • edge proxy
      • Proxy located at boundary of cluster
      • Does TLS termination, routing, filtering
      • istio ingress gateway is edge proxy
    • load balancer
      • distributes requests across ingress gateway pods.
      • provides stable public IP or DNS name
      • cloud providers create it automatically
    • Request flow:
      • user send req to public domain send
      • DNS resolve domain to public domain
      • load balancer forward req to ingress gateway
      • Gateway evaluate gateway resource
      • Virtual service determine routing rules
      • Request reach service and pods
  • Istio-ingress gateway architecture
    • Istio-ingress gateway deployment
      • K8s deployment in k8s env
      • This deployment has pods, and these pods contain containers called as “envoy container”.
      • Purpose of istio-ingress gateway is to process incoming traffic.
      • deployed within “istio-system namespace.
      • can be scaled independently from main app.
    • Envoy Proxy
      • Name of high performance proxy used by istio. a proxy that’s part of a software called “envoy” developed by “lyft” company.
      • can be used anywhere as a proxy within istio - as sidecar proxy, as a container proxy within pods, etc.
    • Gateway pods
      • pods running envoy.
      • recieve requests from load balancer, apply gateway &, virtual service rules.
      • can be horizontally scaled.
    • Gateway selectors
      • selectors specific to istio
      • enables multiple gateways in one cluster.
    • Can support multiple ingress gateways, per app.
    • Also supports one dedicated gateway per app.
    • GatewayCRD - for deploying istio
    • other gateway resources :
      • hosts on istio (allowed domains) - server (listener definition) open protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, etc.)wildcard host - to match multiple domains like *.example.com, multiple hosts listeners.Gateway binding (associating Virtual Services w/ gateways), Gateway lifecycle.
        • Gateway binding
          • virtual services references Gateway
          • w/o binding routes don’t apply.

            Istio vs nginx

    • istio provides what nginx provides plus service mesh (secure to service communication), mTLS (mutual TLS protecting traffic from service to service), traffic splitting as we want, observability, w/o modifying app code.

entry.title: Realtime sys vs Rest API
entry.content:
Realtime sys Vs Rest api

  • always rest api better of little latency & is valuable in comparison to open connections like web socket or SSE.
  • real time sys don’t cook on serverless platforms, edge servers, etc.top

  • Rest is the default choice for most applications.
  • GraphQL is useful for frontend flexibility.
    • Frontend flexibility includes:
      • multiple frontends - Web, mobile, admin portal, partner portal.
      • FE very frequently need diff combinations of existing data. user configurable dashboards & reports. deeply connected data models. eg - Github, Shopify, Netflix, Facebook, Reddit.
